## Proof

We evaluate
$$L = \lim_{n\to\infty} \frac{H^{(1)}_0\!\bigl(2\sqrt{(n+1)x}\bigr)}{H^{(1)}_0\!\bigl(2\sqrt{nx}\bigr)}, \qquad x>0.$$

Set $z_n = 2\sqrt{nx}$, so $z_n \to \infty$ as $n\to\infty$, and $z_{n+1} = 2\sqrt{(n+1)x}$.

**Asymptotic expansion.** For $z\to\infty$ with $|\arg z|<\pi$, the Hankel function of the first kind of order $0$ has the well-known expansion (Olver/Watson):
$$H^{(1)}_0(z) \sim \sqrt{\frac{2}{\pi z}}\, e^{i(z-\pi/4)}\left(1 + \frac{i}{8z} - \frac{9}{128\,z^2} + O(z^{-3})\right).$$
Writing $H^{(1)}_0(z) = \sqrt{\frac{2}{\pi z}}\,e^{i(z-\pi/4)}\bigl(1 + \varepsilon(z)\bigr)$ with $\varepsilon(z) = O(1/z)$, the ratio becomes
$$\frac{H^{(1)}_0(z_{n+1})}{H^{(1)}_0(z_n)} = \sqrt{\frac{z_n}{z_{n+1}}}\;\exp\!\bigl(i(z_{n+1}-z_n)\bigr)\;\frac{1+\varepsilon(z_{n+1})}{1+\varepsilon(z_n)}.$$

We analyze each factor as $n\to\infty$.

**Factor 1 (amplitude).**
$$\sqrt{\frac{z_n}{z_{n+1}}} = \left(\frac{\sqrt{nx}}{\sqrt{(n+1)x}}\right)^{1/2} = \left(\frac{n}{n+1}\right)^{1/4} = \left(1-\frac{1}{n+1}\right)^{1/4}\xrightarrow[n\to\infty]{}1.$$

**Factor 2 (phase).**
$$z_{n+1}-z_n = 2\sqrt{x}\bigl(\sqrt{n+1}-\sqrt{n}\bigr) = \frac{2\sqrt{x}}{\sqrt{n+1}+\sqrt{n}} \sim \frac{\sqrt{x}}{\sqrt{n}} \xrightarrow[n\to\infty]{}0.$$
Hence $\exp\!\bigl(i(z_{n+1}-z_n)\bigr) \to e^{0} = 1$.

**Factor 3 (asymptotic-series correction).** Since $z_n\to\infty$ and $z_{n+1}\to\infty$, we have $\varepsilon(z_n)\to 0$ and $\varepsilon(z_{n+1})\to 0$, so
$$\frac{1+\varepsilon(z_{n+1})}{1+\varepsilon(z_n)} \to \frac{1+0}{1+0}=1.$$

**Combining.** All three factors tend to $1$, so
$$L = 1\cdot 1\cdot 1 = 1.$$

**Remark on the domain.** For $x>0$ both arguments are real and positive, placing us squarely in the sector $|\arg z|<\pi$ where the standard large-$z$ expansion of $H^{(1)}_0$ is valid. (For $x=0$ the arguments vanish and $Y_0$ diverges logarithmically, so the expression is undefined; the natural domain of the problem is $x>0$.)

$$\boxed{\displaystyle \lim_{n\to\infty} \frac{H^{(1)}_0\!\bigl(2\sqrt{(n+1)x}\bigr)}{H^{(1)}_0\!\bigl(2\sqrt{nx}\bigr)} = 1,\qquad x>0.}$$
